content.text: Have you ever applied to dozens of jobs online, only to hear absolute silence in return? It is incredibly frustrating, but here is a secret: it is probably not your skills that are the problem. It is the robot gatekeeper! Over 95% of major companies use a software tool called an **Applicant Tracking System (ATS)** to screen resumes. If your resume is not structured correctly, the ATS filters you out before a human ever gets to see your name.

To beat this, you need an **ATS-friendly resume**. Think of it as formatting your CV so the computer can read it smoothly. If you are starting completely from scratch, check out our guide on [how to write a resume](/blog/how-to-make-a-resume) to get your basic sections down first.
Why Does Being ATS-Friendly Matter So Much?

Recruiters receive hundreds of applications for a single job opening. They do not have time to read every single one. Instead, the ATS scans the text of your resume and looks for specific keywords that match the job description. If your resume is full of complex columns, tables, or icons, the parser gets confused and scrambles your text. When that happens, you look unqualified to the system, and your application gets rejected automatically.

content.text: The Checklist: Make Your Resume Pass Every Scan

items: **Stick to a Single Column:** Parsers read left-to-right. Two-column templates look cool but scramble the reading order for bots.
**Use Clean Headers:** Stick to standard titles like 'Professional Experience', 'Education', and 'Skills'. Creative titles confuse the scanner.

**Optimize Your Keywords:** Make sure you use the exact terms from the job post. Check out our [resume skills examples](/blog/resume-skills-examples) to see how to list your technical and soft skills correctly.
**No Graphics or Tables:** Keep images, charts, and progress bars off your resume. Scanners see them as empty blocks.

faqs.question: What is an ATS-friendly resume?
faqs.answer: It is a resume that uses simple formatting, standard fonts, clear headings, and relevant keywords so Applicant Tracking Systems can read it without errors.

faqs.question: Can I use color on my resume?
faqs.answer: Yes, color is fine. The scanning software reads the text characters, not color. Just avoid charts, graphics, and multi-column tables.

faqs.question: How do I know if my resume is readable by an ATS?
faqs.answer: A quick test is to copy all text from your PDF (Ctrl+A) and paste it into Notepad. If the text pastes in a logical reading order without spelling errors or merged words, it is readable.
